hypothesis: On X = {0,1}^4 with orbit-canonical screens q_G, exact representability of a task Y occurs iff model symmetry is contained in target symmetry (G_M ⊆ G_Y). Under-repair makes Y unrepresentable. Over-repair remains representable but has strictly more fibres (16 vs 5 on popcount). Exact repair must split mixed fibres. Delete-then-default and relative-then-drop disagree. A 4-cycle of integer steps closes iff the steps sum to 0, and two potentials differ by a constant.

controls.description: No PRNG, SGD, or neural training. Every gate is a deterministic finite enumeration or an integer identity on the 16-point cube and two declared 4-cycles.
G_Y is computed as {g in S_4 : Y(g x) = Y(x) for all 16 x}, not assumed from a closed form except as a regression target.
Y is representable from q iff Y is constant on every q-fibre. For orbit-canonical q_G this is checked against G ⊆ G_Y on the 4×4 grid.
The sorted-tuple map q_perm and the popcount histogram induce the same five fibres; asserted in tests.
A constant dummy repair is not an ExactRepair of q_perm for first_bit; the split gate fails closed if this negative control is accepted.
DTA_NONCOMMUTE requires both a sequence pair that agrees on Path A and disagrees on Path B and the Lean (0,1)/(1,1) pair regression.
Holonomy is checked on a declared zero-sum 4-cycle and a declared nonzero-sum 4-cycle, plus potential uniqueness up to a constant on both.

gates.criterion: Every (model, task) with G_M notsubseteq G_Y is unrepresentable: Y is not constant on q_M-fibres.
Every (model, task) with G_M ⊆ G_Y is representable: Y is constant on q_M-fibres.
On popcount, q_id has 16 fibres and q_perm has 5 fibres, and 16 > 5 (leftover privilege, not a no-go).
For first_bit, the Stab(0) orbit map is representable, q_perm is not, and G_rot ∩ G_first = {e} so q_rot is not representable.
At least one q_perm fibre mixes first-bit values; r = first_bit is an ExactRepair and splits every leftover disagreement; a constant r is not.
There exist two states that agree on Path A (drop index 0, write 0) and disagree on Path B (remember x[1]-x[0], drop absolute), including the Lean pair (0,1) vs (1,1).
A 4-cycle of Int steps closes iff the steps sum to 0 (zero-sum cycle closes; nonzero-sum cycle does not); two potentials for the same steps differ by a constant.
